question: Should OpenClaw core adopt ordered, immutable startup configuration layers as a supported Gateway contract?
rationale: The PR creates a durable core CLI and configuration lifecycle surface for managed hosts; code review can identify defects, but it cannot decide whether core should permanently own that product contract while the RFC remains open.

options.title: Sponsor and repair
options.body: Adopt the startup-only contract, require the write guard to be path-scoped, and add writable-profile coexistence proof before merge.

options.title: Hold for RFC
options.body: Keep the PR open but pause implementation review until the managed-configuration RFC settles precedence, lifecycle, and ownership semantics.

options.title: Decline core ownership
options.body: Keep composition in the host launcher and close the core PR if maintainers do not want this CLI and lifecycle contract in OpenClaw.

recommendation.title: Sponsor and repair
recommendation.body: Adopt the startup-only contract, require the write guard to be path-scoped, and add writable-profile coexistence proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans the Gateway CLI, configuration architecture, operator lifecycle, and the repository's lean-core product boundary.
